grand_strategy.reading: Iceland is a NATO state with no army whose security rests on Washington, and in 2026 that dependence became a source of friction: after Trump's Davos gaffe and the September map post, Reykjavík summoned the US ambassador but did not change course. Its answer to the EU question is the same caution: Icelanders voted on 29 August 2026 not to restart accession talks, and the government set membership aside until 2028 while keeping the EEA. The Arctic role grows through NATO and the UK-led Joint Expeditionary Force rather than through forces of its own. Open gaps: the outcome of the US force-posture review and the size of the US presence at Keflavík were not found.

stances.note: The 1951 defence arrangement and the Keflavík presence make the United States the guarantor of Iceland, which has no army. In 2025-26 Washington's Greenland push and the Davos and map posts turned the protector into a source of pressure: Reykjavík summoned Ambassador Billy Long on 7 September 2026, and Prime Minister Frostadóttir called the post an insult to Icelanders, Canadians and Greenlanders. No source uses the word 'reluctant'; the grade is our reading of a NATO co-member that stays aligned while visibly resisting Washington (confidence B, because the alignment and the friction are both sourced). Bond - affinity: shared Atlantic and Western ties rather than kinship.

stances.note: Iceland aligns itself completely with EU sanctions on Russia and suspended its embassy operations in Moscow on 1 August 2023. Its own concern is structural: suspected shadow-fleet vessels operate inside its exclusive economic zone (outside the 12-mile zone), and the telecom cables that link the island are watched more closely. No source uses the word 'rival' or 'adversary'. The grade is our reading (confidence C): no declared aim of Russia's defeat, and no Russian incursion into Icelandic airspace was found for 2026. Bond - none: no kinship and no historic wound with Russia.

stances.note: Iceland is not an EU member: it stays in the EEA and passport-free Schengen, and the government has set the membership question aside until 2028 after the 29 August 2026 referendum (52.8% no on restarting talks). The EU is therefore a partner for a non-member, transactional and treaty-based, not an ally. Trend stable: the referendum closes accession for now but leaves the EEA framework untouched. Bond - none: pure interest (market access, fisheries, the EEA). The since date marks the EEA framework (in force 1994); the cited sources do not state it, so it is our dating.
